title: Leverich Helio Stewardship IRSC
description: Sources Sought (SS) / Request for Information (RFI) This Sources Sought / Request for Information (RFI) is issued solely for market research and planning purposes. It does not constitute a solicitation or a promise to issue a solicitation in the future. The Government will not reimburse accompanying costs. Any answers or attachments provided are based upon the best information available at the time of the visit and are subject to change. 1. Background & Purpose USDA Forest Service seeks capability statements from qualified vendors able to conduct fuels reduction on steep and rugged terrain within Bozeman Municipal Watershed Project area for the anticipated Leverich Helio Stewardship IRSC. The purpose of this SS/RFI is to gather information on vendor capabilities, invite prospective vendors to an organized site visit on 10/01/2026, and to view the area before snow limits access. 2. Anticipated Scope of Work Cut and removal of approximately 290 CCF of Lodgepole pine sawtimber 2045 CCF of Douglas-fir and other Sawtimber on 151 acres. Whole-tree Helicopter yarding of included timber. Piling of slash at the landing area. Road Decommissioning of .59 miles of existing Temporary Road Use Permit (TRUP) roads post-hauling. 3. Place of Performance The Leverich Helio Stewardship IRSC project is located in the northern Gallatin Mountain Range, just south of Bozeman, MT. Helicopter units are located on the west side of FS Road #979, along Bozeman Creek and adjacent to City of Bozeman land. 4. Period of Performance Anticipated start date: Late Spring/Early Summer 2027. Period of performance is estimated to not exceed two operational seasons and is dependent on weather, access, and coordination. 5. Site Visit An organized site visit will occur on Thursday, October 1, 2026, at 10:00 a.m. MDT. Interested parties will meet at the Bozeman Ranger District located at 3710 Fallon St. Suite C. Bozeman, MT 59718. Interested parties should contact Nathan Motzko at nathan.motzko@usda.gov or 406-224-0323 by 12:00 p.m. MDT on September 30, 2026, if they intend to attend. 6. Requested Capability Statement Content Company information (UEI, address, email, POC, socio-economic status). Relevant experience, especially hazardous fuel reduction, helicopter yarding, steep slope timber operations. Safety program details and crew qualifications. Equipment lists and mobilization capabilities. Past performance references. 7. Response Instructions & Due Date Any information submitted by vendors to this this SS/RFI is voluntary. Responses should be submitted electronically to Jeanne Windle at norma.windle@usda.gov. All responses are due no later than October 15, 2026, at 4:00 p.m. MDT. 8. Points of Contact Direct all questions via email to Jeanne Windle, Contracting Officer at norma.windle@usda.gov.

title: Centrum současného umění a architektury (Dům umění) – rekonstrukce objektu – Etapa I
description: Objednatel (město České Budějovice) se rozhodl zrealizovat rekonstrukci „Domu umění“ a vytvořit zde Centrum současného umění a architektury (CSUA), na které má již zpracovanou projektovou dokumentaci do stupně provedení stavby z 07/2023 s platností povolení stavby do 5ti let od nabytí právní moci. Vzhledem k limitovaným finančním zdrojům objednatele a k významnému nárůstu předpokládaných nákladů stavby v čase, zejména v důsledku inflace a vývoje cen stavebních prací a dodávek od ukončení soutěže o návrh v roce 2021, je objednatel nucen realizaci stavby rozdělit do dvou etap. Tato změna investičního záměru je reflektována v rozdělení a úpravě původní dokumentace tak, že umožňuje realizaci stavby v etapách při zachování bezpečnosti, provozuschopnosti a funkčnosti 1. etapy. Z hlediska nosné konstrukce a obálky bude stavba zrealizována celá. Cílovým stavem 1. etapy je plné zprovoznění 1. a 2. nadzemního podlaží objektu, včetně všech nezbytných stavebních a technických opatření potřebných pro bezpečný a řádný provoz této části stavby. Vyšší patra, tedy 3.-5. nadzemní podlaží, budou v rámci 1. etapy ponechána ve stavu hrubé stavby s přípravou napojovacích bodů TZB pro budoucí vestavbu (tzv. „shell and core“). Jelikož je terasa v 5.NP součástí obálky a z hlediska požární bezpečnosti je možné ji zpřístupnit, je i ta součástí Etapy 1. Předmětem plnění veřejné zakázky je zrealizovat dílo pod názvem „Centrum současného umění a architektury“ (Dům umění) – rekonstrukce objektu“ vymezené projektovou dokumentací pod názvem „DUCB – DŮM UMĚNÍ ČESKÉ BUDĚJOVICE – DPS ETAPA I., zpracované projekční kanceláří Malý Chmel s.r.o. se sídlem Jungmannova 697/46, České Budějovice 7, 370 01 České Budějovice, IČO: 09674411. Jedná se o kompletní rekonstrukci objektu, která zahrnuje zejména bourací práce, úpravy dle architektonicko stavebního a stavebně konstrukčního řešení, provedení nové techniky prostředí staveb (zdravotně technické instalace; silnoproudé a slaboproudé rozvody – EPS, EZS, data a světelná technika, stabilní hasící zařízení; vzduchotechnika a chlazení; vytápění; měření a regulace) a provedení provizorních opatření pro zajištění prostor, které budou realizovány v ETAPĚ 2.

description: Derby City Council (the Council) is undertaking this procurement to establish two contracts: • Lot 1 Asbestos removal and remediation services • Lot 2 Asbestos analyst services The procurement process adopted by the Council is based on the 'Open' tendering procedure as detailed in the Procurement Act 2023 (the "Act") and the Procurement Regulations 2024 (the "Regulations".) For Lot 1 the asbestos removal and remediation services contract, the initial contract period is two years and is estimated to commence on 1st February 2027 and expire on 31st January 2029. For Lot 2 the asbestos analyst services contract, the initial contract period is two years and is estimated to commence on 13th February 2027 and expire on 12th February 2029. For both contracts there will be an option to extend the contract for three (3) years in annual increments, subject to satisfactory performance and business needs. Maximum contract period is five (5) years. Local Government Reorganisation (LGR) is underway in several areas across the country and may result in changes to council structures, service delivery and responsibilities, and geographical coverage during the life of the contract. For this contract it is anticipated that the effects of LGR may lead to an increased service demand or the need to extend provision to new areas or client groups. For Lot 1 the asbestos removal and remediation services contract, bidders should note that the total estimated contract value of £1,172,000, comprises of two components: i) The core contract value, estimated at £293,000, based on known current service requirements ii) An additional estimated value of £879,000 to reflect potential future changes in service scope or volume linked to LGR. For Lot 2 the asbestos analyst services contract, bidders should note that the total estimated contract value of £2,616,000, comprises of two components: i) The core contract value, estimated at £654,000, based on known current service requirements ii) An additional estimated value of £1,962,000 to reflect potential future changes in service scope or volume linked to LGR. These figures are estimations and due to only being in the early stages of the process the Authority cannot give any commitment on these figures but would like to build scope into the Contract should the need arise.

title: Viittomakielisten tulkkausten ja käännösten hankinta valtioneuvostolle
description: Valtioneuvoston kanslia (VNK) on yksi 12 ministeriöstä. Sen päätehtävä on tukea pääministeriä valtioneuvoston johtamisessa sekä hallituksen ja eduskunnan työn yhteensovittamisessa. VNK vastaa valtioneuvoston toiminnan organisoinnista ja hallituksen toimintaedellytysten järjestämisestä kaikissa olosuhteissa. Hankinnan kohteena ovat valtioneuvoston ja sen ministeriöiden tarvitsemien suomalaisen ja suomenruotsalaisen viittomakielen tulkkaus- ja käännöspalveluiden hankinta. Tulkkaus- ja käännöspalveluita tarvitaan pääsääntöisesti suomesta ja/tai ruotsista suomalaiselle ja suomenruotsalaiselle viittomakielelle, mutta jonkin verran myös suomalaisesta ja suomenruotsalaisesta viittomakielestä suomeksi. Viittomakielisiä tulkkaus- ja käännöspalveluita tarvitaan erityisesti 1.7.2026 valtioneuvoston kansliassa aloittaneen valtioneuvoston viestintäosaston tarpeisiin. Valtioneuvoston viestintäosasto vastaa valtioneuvoston ja sen ministeriöiden viestinnästä ja valtionhallinnon viestinnän yhteensovittamisesta. Suositus viittomakielten käytöstä valtioneuvoston viestinnässä 2025 edistää viittomakielisten kielellisten oikeuksien toteutumista. Viestintään liittyvien tulkkaus- ja käännöspalveluiden lisäksi hankinnan kohteena ovat myös ministeriöiden muut viittomakieliset tulkkaus- ja käännöstarpeet (osa-alueet 5-8), joiden hankinnassa valtioneuvoston kanslia toimii hankintarenkaan vetäjänä ja hankintarenkaassa ovat mukana liikenne- ja viestintäministeriö, oikeusministeriö, opetus- ja kulttuuriministeriö, sosiaali- ja terveysministeriö, ulkoministeriö ja valtiovarainministeriö sekä oikeuskanslerinvirasto. Tulkkaukset ja käännökset voivat koskea mitä tahansa ministeriöiden toimialoihin kuuluvaa asiaa, ks. valtioneuvoston ohjesääntö 262/2003, § 10–24, https://www.finlex.fi/fi/laki/ajantasa/2003/20030262. Lisätietoa ministeriöiden toiminnasta on saatavilla ministeriöiden www-sivustoilla, ks. https://valtioneuvosto.fi/ministeriot Hankinta on EU-kynnysarvon ylittävä palveluhankinta ja se on jaettu kahdeksaan osa-alueeseen: 1. Tiedotustilaisuuksien tulkkaukset suomesta suomalaiselle viittomakielelle 2. Tiedotustilaisuuksien tulkkaukset suomesta ja ruotsista suomenruotsalaiselle viittomakielelle 3. Viestintään liittyvät käännökset suomesta suomalaiselle viittomakielelle 4. Viestintään liittyvät käännökset ruotsista suomenruotsalaiselle viittomakielelle 5. Muut tulkkaukset suomesta suomalaiselle viittomakielelle ja suomalaisesta viittomakielestä suomeksi 6. Muut tulkkaukset suomesta ja ruotsista suomenruotsalaiselle viittomakielelle ja suomenruotsalaisesta viittomakielestä suomeksi ja ruotsiksi 7. Muut käännökset suomesta suomalaiselle viittomakielelle 8. Muut käännökset ruotsista suomenruotsalaiselle viittomakielelle Tarjoaja voi tehdä tarjouksen yhdelle tai useammalle osa-alueelle. Kullekin osa-alueelle perustetaan puitejärjestely, jossa valitut toimittajat on asetettu etusijajärjestykseen. Hankinnan ennakoitu arvo on kaikki kielet yhteenlaskettuna noin 100 000 euroa/vuosi. Valittavien toimittajien kanssa tehdään kahden vuoden (24 kk) puitesopimus, joka sisältää kaksi yhden (1) vuoden optiota. Sopimuskauden arvioitu alkamisajankohta on 1.11.2026., 1. title: APN - Housing Construction Plan
description: Advance Procurement Notice Housing Construction plan Purpose of this Advance Procurement Notice This is not a bid solicitation nor a request for proposals. This is an advance notice for potential contracts to provide interested Design-Builders an opportunity to learn about the upcoming housing construction program. Note that there is no guarantee that these solicitations will proceed. Description of the Program and Services The Canadian Forces Housing Agency (CFHA) is planning a Housing Program to support the delivery of new residential housing for members of the Canadian Armed Forces at bases and wings across Canada. CFHA is responsible for the provision and management of military housing on Department of National Defence (DND) lands, and this program supports ongoing efforts to modernize and expand the housing portfolio to meet current and future operational needs. The objective of the program is to deliver new housing efficiently and at speed through Modified Design -Build (MDB) delivery model that integrates studies, design and construction under a single contract. The services required under this program include: Architectural & Engineering (A&E) services for the provision site studies, planning and detailed design development and all associated works. Design and construction of new infrastructure and housing to support the residential housing program. Note that certain locations may involve phased delivery. Planned building types will emphasize higher-density development, primarily mid-rise apartment buildings. The proposed number of units at each location is subject to adjustment as requirements are finalized. It is anticipated that each location will be delivered under its own Modified Design-Build (MDB) contract. However, subject to change, certain locations may be bundled and procured through a single Request for Proposals (RFP), as outlined below in no particular order. Location / Proposed Number of Housing Units / Estimated Design and Construction Costs ($M) RFP No.1 (Published) Comox, British Columbia/ 212 units/ $96M Esquimalt, British Columbia/ 200 units/ $91M RFP No.2 (Published) Ottawa, Ontario/ 280 units/ $128M RFP No.3 (Published) Yellowknife, Northwest Territories/ 32 units / $15M RFP No.4 (Published) Gagetown, New Brunswick/ 656 units / $323M Greenwood, Nova Scotia/ 208 units / $95M Halifax, Nova Scotia/ 400 units /$182M RFP No.5 (Published) Montreal, Quebec/ 200 units/ $91M Valcartier, Quebec/ 1120 units/ $510M Bagotville, Quebec/240 units/ $109M It is anticipated that the following solicitations related to this program will be initiated in Fall 2026. This is conditional on receiving approval to proceed by the Department of National Defence (DND). RFP No.6 Wainwright, Alberta/ 94 units/ $43M Cold Lake, Alberta/ 232 units/ $106M Edmonton, Alberta/ 1010 units/ $459M RFP No.7 Winnipeg, Manitoba/ 240 units/ $110M Shilo, Manitoba/ 184 units/ $84M RFP No.8 Borden, Ontario/ 210 units / $96M Kingston, Ontario/ 960 units/ $437M North Bay, Ontario/ 78 units/ $36M Petawawa, Ontario/ 1114 units/ $507M RFP No.9 Moose Jaw, Saskatchewan/ 24 units/ $11M The Government of Canada is committed to advancing reconciliation and fostering meaningful engagement with Indigenous Peoples. In alignment with these commitments, the Department of National Defence (DND) seeks to create opportunities for Indigenous businesses and communities through (sub)contracting, employment, and training initiatives associated with the proposed program of work. It is anticipated that Indigenous communities will benefit from potential subcontracting, employment, and training opportunities arising from this program of work. Questions Any questions relating to this Advance Procurement Notice can be addressed to: Antoine am Rhyn Regional Service Line Leader, Contract Services Defence Construction Canada 819-431-7650 Antoine.amrhyn@dcc-cdc.gc.ca    Bidding and Documents are available on http://www.merx.com. Fees may apply; See https://www.merx.com/public/pricing for more information.

description: The purpose of the Public Contract is the redevelopment of the TIR Centre, an exceptional logistics site composed of land and buildings located less than 3 km from the heart of Brussels. title: Netherlands – Payroll management services – Europees openbare aanbesteding Salarisadministratie Dienstverlening
description: De salarisadministratie is momenteel uitbesteed aan een externe partij, die deze werkzaamheden uitvoert voor circa 10 tot 12 uur per week en, indien nodig, ad hoc consultancydiensten. Deze partij is verantwoordelijk voor de periodieke salarisverwerking en aanverwante werkzaamheden zoals beschreven in Bijlage F – Werkzaamheden. De personeelsadministratie is ondergebracht binnen team HR, onderdeel van de afdeling HR & Organisatieontwikkeling en wordt uitgevoerd door drie parttime medewerkers. Zij zijn verantwoordelijk voor het aanleveren, controleren en verwerken van verschillende personeelsmutaties. Sinds januari 2023 wordt gewerkt met het systeem AFAS. Een groot deel van de HR- en salarisprocessen is ingericht via workflows binnen dit systeem. Dit zorgt voor een gestructureerde en gedigitaliseerde werkwijze, maar vraagt ook om specifieke systeemkennis en ondersteuning. Deze opdracht is een raamovereenkomst met een totale geraamde waarde van € 203.000,- exclusief BTW over de gehele duur van de overeenkomst van 4 jaar (incl. verlengopties).

title: USACE National Enterprise Dredging Center Scope Dredge to Budget Contract
description: Special Notice: W912PM27RA006 Title: Virtual Industry Day for FY27 USACE Enterprise Dredge Delivery Center Scope Dredge to Budget The Virtual Industry Day Meeting for the USACE Enterprise Dredge Delivery Center Scope Dredge to Budget will occur on 16 October 2026 from 0900ET to 13:00ET via Teams. All interested dredging companies are encouraged to attend. During the meeting, we will be discussing Scope Dredge to Budget acquisition strategy. Scope Dredge to Budget: Optimize the Budget in terms of quality, scope, durability with innovative betterments and betterments within the budget. The goal of the scope-dredge to budget is maximizing achievable scope within a target budget that will be provided in the solicitation. The Enterprise Dredge Delivery Center intends to issue 1 solicitation for the Galveston/Houston Area of Responsibility. Phase One -A technical qualifications-based evaluation of initial proposals -RFP that defines the project with functional and performance requirements, budget cap, and schedule/delivery requirements -A statement of the maximum number of offerors that will be selected to submit Phase 2 proposals. -RFO FAR 36.101-2(b)(4) states maximum number of offerors shall not exceed five (5) Phase One proposals from vendors do not include: -Detailed design information -Cost or price information Down-select Decision for most highly qualified offerors in accordance with the solicitation. Proposed Phase 1 Qualifications -Proof of bonding capacity -Past Performance -Proposed Plant Proprietary Meetings (RFO FAR 15.101 Exchanges with Industry before receipt of proposals) Phase Two in accordance with FAR 15 Source Selection Procedures to determine best value. Official Phase Two RFP issued by amendment for most highly qualified offerors to submit phase-two competitive proposals that include technical proposals and cost or price information. Proposed Phase 2 Evaluation Factors -Maximum amount of time to maintain the channels at authorized dimensions -Maximum use of beneficial use -Schedule -Management Approach The harbors to be dredged include the Sabine-Neches Waterway, Galveston Harbor & Channel, Houston Ship Channel, Texas City Ship Channel, Freeport Harbor, Matagorda Ship Channel, Corpus Christi Ship Channel, Brazos Island Harbor, Gulf Intracoastal Waterway & Tributaries, Channel to Victoria, and Channel to Harlington. See Attachment 1 for project descriptions and map. Please RSVP no later than 10AM ET 15 October 2026 to both Ros Shoemaker and Terri Adams at Rosalind.m.shoemaker@usace.army.mil and terri.m.adams@usace.army.mil if you plan to attend the Industry Day. A Teams calendar invite will be sent out to all RSVP�s. Industry is also encouraged to provide any feedback on the proposed acquisition strategies or contract pairings. Feedback can be provided via email to the contracting officer and contract specialist listed above. If you would like to provide any questions in advance of the meeting, please provide them no later than 10AM ET, 08 September 2026.

title: NISC Enterprise Support Tasking (NEST)
description: ***THIS OPPORTUNITY IS SET-ASIDE FOR WOMEN-OWNED SMALL BUSINESS (WOSB) CONCERNS*** **A LIVE NIMS DEMONSTRATION WILL OCCUR 09 SEP 2026, SEE L.8 FOR DETAILS** The AJW-2 Directorate, AJW-2131 Implementation Services Group, provides technical, engineering, financial, budget, and management support to Technical Operations programs using the NAS Integration Support Contract (NISC IV Contract) and Technical Support Services Contract (TSSC).These are task order contracts that present contract managers with the task of managing the entire Task Order Management lifecycle, the Financial Management lifecycle encompassing the obligation and de-obligation of funds by integrating with FAA�s financial systems, PRISM and Delphi and the Invoice/Payments lifecycle. The NISC IV contract will also be transitioned to NISC V contract during the award period, which will require a new system to support the NISC V contract, while maintaining the NIMS system to close out the NISC IV contract. This work requires a support contractor that will provide Operations and Maintenance services for the NIMS systems that is used to manage the current NISC IV contract using the existing technology stack and will provide quality assurance and quality control to ensure uninterrupted system availability. In addition, the vendor should maintain and run reports if required from CMIS system that was used to support the NISC III contract and is currently not active. The work also requires the vendor to serve as a Subject Matter Expert (SME) capable of providing design, development, testing, deployment and documentation of the new software that will be required to support the NISC V contract when required. This includes, but is not limited to, making recommendations regarding the selection of software architecture and software development tools that will be required to develop the new system. The Contractor must provide operations and maintenance support for the NIMS/CMIS system, provide quality assurance and quality control, provide security compliance and ensure uninterrupted system availability. This effort also requires the vendor to serve as a SME and provide support with system architecture, software recommendations, system design, development, testing, deployment, and documentation for a new system to support NISC V contract requirements when required. Contractor will maintain NIMS/CMIS security certifications required to operate the software and its associated server hardware. The Contractor must also provide transition support to any potential new vendor at the contract�s end. ***THIS OPPORTUNITY IS SET-ASIDE FOR WOMEN-OWNED SMALL BUSINESS (WOSB) CONCERNS*** **A LIVE NIMS DEMONSTRATION WILL OCCUR 09 SEP 2026, SEE L.8 FOR DETAILS**

title: J045--Sources Sought/RFI, Including Industry Days WV VA Medical Centers Facility Maintenance & Repairs BPA RFI Clarksburg, Beckley, and Huntington WV VAMC Mechanical, Plumbing, and Electrical Systems
description: Sources Sought Notice Sources Sought Notice Page 9 of 9 Sources Sought Notice *= Required Field Sources Sought Notice Page 1 of 2 General Summary: Department of Veterans Affairs, Veterans Health Administration, Network Contracting Office 5 (NCO 5), is issuing this request for information/sources sought notice in order to identify vendors that are interested in and capable of providing maintenance, repair, and replacement of Plumbing Systems, HVAC-R Systems, Mechanical Systems, Electrical Systems, and Control Systems at VA Medical Centers located in Beckley, Clarksburg, and Huntington WV. Primary locations are the Beckley VA Medical Center, Louis A. Johnson VA Medical Center (Clarksburg), and Hershel "Woody" Williams VA Medical Center (Huntington). Additional information on VA facilities can be found at https://www.va.gov/find-locations/ . Description of Work: Multiple firm-fixed unit price Blanket Purchase Agreements (BPAs) will be established to provide Mechanical, Electrical, and Plumbing (MEP) repair and maintenance services across Beckley VA Medical Center, Louis A. Johnson VA Medical Center (Clarksburg), Hershel "Woody" Williams VA Medical Center (Huntington), and with a surge capacity to service all associated clinics. The contractor shall furnish all necessary qualified personnel, supervision, materials, equipment, and services to perform the tasks in the Statement of Work prepared for each Task Order. The scope encompasses maintenance, repair, and replacement of the systems below. Mechanical Systems HVAC-R Systems Supply, return, and exhaust ductwork (testing, repair, installation, demolition) Direct Digital Controls Variable Speed Drives (including ABB drives) Electric motors, fans, actuators VAV and CAV boxes Coil cleaning, repair, replacement Air conditioning, DX Cooling, VRF systems Chillers, air handlers, compressors, fan coils, heat exchangers, heat pumps, humidifiers, dehumidifiers TAB (testing, adjusting, and air balancing) Filter servicing and cleaning Exhaust fan repairs HVAC-R system demolition Area and room pressure monitoring and testing Temperature/humidity monitoring systems, sensors, transmitters, base stations (troubleshooting, repair, replacement) Exhaust hoods and exhaust systems (troubleshooting, repair, replacement) Equipment and Specialty Systems Maintenance Warehouse dock levelers and garage doors: troubleshoot, repair, replace all associated systems Laundry equipment: troubleshooting, repair, and replacement of all laundry systems, including electronics and controls Grounds equipment: troubleshooting, repair, and replacement Medical and Facility Mechanical Systems Medical air and vacuum systems Dental air and vacuum systems and traps Medical bulk oxygen systems Air compressors Walk-in coolers/freezers, medical refrigerators/freezers Kitchen refrigeration equipment repairs Electrical Systems Repair, maintenance, and replacement of electrical infrastructure, including: Power generators and generator control systems Transformers, transmission lines, and conduits (above and below grade) Electrical panels, breakers, fuses, circuits Switches, relays, outlets, lamps, bulbs (standard and LED), and general electrical gear Elevator support systems (electrical aspects) Switchgear, troubleshooting, repair, replacement Automatic transfer switches (ATS), troubleshooting, repair, replacement Roadway lighting systems, troubleshooting, repair, replacement Uninterrupted Power Supply (UPS) systems, troubleshooting, repair, and replacement Above and underground fuel tanks and associated systems (troubleshooting, repair, replacement) Plumbing Systems Maintenance, repair, and replacement of: Drain, waste, and vent systems Compressed gas system components (air, oxygen, vacuum) Medical gas analysis and certification Leak repair Pipe insulation and labeling Sewer and storm drain systems Unplugging and servicing toilets, urinals, sinks, and showers Grease trap and sump pump servicing Steam system testing, repair, and demolition Heating hot water/chilled water loops, water balancing Underground fire line, irrigation line, building drain, sewer, and domestic water piping and valves Excavation for repairs/replacement Backflow device testing and repair Plumbing fixture installation, replacement, repair, or removal Emergency eye wash and shower repair or replacement Pressure vessel installation, certification, and repair Steam system components (traps, valves, pumps) Water pumps, reverse osmosis stations, water softeners, chlorination stations, water filters Plumbing demolition Licensing & Warranty Requirements: The prime contractor must hold valid West Virginia contractor licenses for Plumbing and HVAC-R. All prime and subcontractor personnel must have appropriate licensures and certifications. All materials, equipment, software, and labor provided must be warranted by the prime contractor for one year from operational start. All facility parts, materials, or software must be approved by the VA prior to installation; obsolete or proprietary systems are not permitted. All work products and project bid information created under this contract becomes the sole intellectual property of the VA. Period Of Performance and Value: Multiple straight 5-year Blanket Purchase Agreements (BPAs) will be awarded, each consisting of five ordering periods. These BPAs will facilitate the issuance of firm fixed price BPA call orders over a total period of five years. Task Orders will be project-specific, with most expected to range between $10,001 and $100,000, and an individual Task Order ceiling of approximately $300,000. The total estimated contract capacity over the life of the BPA is projected to be $9,000,000. title: Sepsis Research Blood Sample Collection Services
description: Notice of Intent (NOI) to Sole Source Title: Sepsis Research Blood Sample Collection Services Requiring Activity: Walter Reed Army Institute of Research (WRAIR), Integrative Systems Biology (ISB) Branch Related Notice: HT942523P0084 Product Service Code (PSC): AN11 - HEALTH R&D SERVICES; HEALTH CARE SERVICES; BASIC RESEARCH North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) Code: 541714 - Research and Development in Biotechnology (except Nanobiotechnology) Small Business Size Standard: 1000 employees The Defense Health Agency Contracting Activity (DHACA) on behalf of the Integrative Systems Biology (ISB) Branch at the Walter Reed Army Institute of Research (WRAIR) intends to extend current contract services as a cost R&D contract on a sole source basis to Medstar Health Research Institute, Inc. (MHRI), 10980 Grantchester Way 7th Fl, Columbia, MD 21044-6097 USA; Cage Code 3J1M2 under the RFO FAR 6.103-1 � Only one responsible source can supply the required products due to the non-commercially available sources of the blood samples the Government is requesting. Description of Requirement: This is a requirement to extend and re-structure a Firm-Fixed Price contract into a Research and Development (R&D) cost type contract vehicle that will allow the Integrative Systems Biology (ISB) Branch to procure samples from septic and non-septic burn patients along with longitudinal clinical data for the assessment of biomarkers of sepsis for refinement and validation of SeptiBurnAlert program. These blood samples; to include longitudinal clinical data, are currently being collected by MHRI in accordance with an approved Institutional Review Board (IRB) protocol and are actively recruiting subjects for patient samples that meet the specific thermally injured criteria. The Government will convert the current contract from a firm fixed price award to a cost type, RFO part 35 R&D contract to better align the requirement with the Government�s needs. This special notice of intent is not a request for competitive proposals, and no solicitation document exists for this requirement. Meaningful submissions received in response to this notice will be considered solely for the purpose of determining whether competitive procurement is in the best interest of the Government. If no meaningful, written submissions are received by the date listed below, after the publication of this notice, the solicitation will be issued as a sole source requirement to Medstar Health Research Institute, Inc. Based on the above information, the only technically acceptable vendor to fulfill this requirement is MHRI. Submit capability statements (using PDF, MS Word, or Excel attachments) to Ms. Nicole Applegate at e-mail: nicole.v.applegate.civ@health.mil Capability statements are due no later than 10:00am Eastern Time on October 15, 2026.

title: Industry Day U.S. Merchant Marine Academy Campus Modernization
description: FALL FY27 INDUSTRY DAY U.S. Merchant Marine Academy Campus Modernization Industry Day Special Notice | Thursday, October 15, 2026 Event Overview The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), New York District, and the U.S. Merchant Marine Academy (USMMA) will host the Fall FY27 Industry Day from 11:00 a.m. to 2:00 p.m. Eastern Time on October 15, 2026. The hybrid event will bring industry, government, community organizations, and other interested attendees together with USMMA and USACE leadership for an updated view of the Campus Modernization Initiative, its strategic direction, and anticipated procurement activity. This event is open to the general public, and interested vendors. The FY27-FY28 forecast will emphasize the substantial heavy construction opportunities central to the modernization program while also addressing utility upgrades and complementary supporting and non-construction requirements. In-person participation is strongly encouraged. Prior registration is required for every attendee and closes at 12:00 p.m. Eastern Time on October 12, 2026. Event Information Event: USMMA Campus Modernization Fall FY27 Industry Day Date: Thursday, October 15, 2026 Event Time: 11:00 a.m. to 2:00 p.m. Eastern Time Check-In: Opens at 10:00 a.m.; in-person attendees should arrive no later than 10:45 a.m. to allow at least 15 minutes for networking before the program begins Location: U.S. Merchant Marine Academy, 300 Steamboat Road, Kings Point, NY 11024; enter through the main gate Format: Hybrid; in-person attendance is strongly encouraged. Registered virtual attendees will receive a Microsoft Teams link on October 13, 2026 Audience: All interested attendees age 16 or older (public attendees welcome) Registration Deadline: 12:00 p.m. Eastern Time, Monday, October 12, 2026 Theme: USACE Partnering with Industry and the Local Community Industry Day Highlights The Industry Day program will include the following: Welcome and Keynote Remarks: USACE leadership, USMMA Academy leadership, and invited guests will discuss the modernization program, acquisition approaches, and community impacts. Strategic Program Overview: A general USMMA overview and FY27-FY28 Campus Modernization update, including the strategic vision, updated waterfall chart, and local-government and community considerations. Heavy Construction Forecast: A focused review of the significant heavy construction opportunities expected to drive the modernization program. Specific project names, dollar ranges, and acquisition methods will be presented at the event rather than released in this notice. Supporting and Utility Requirements: Discussion of utility upgrades and complementary non-construction requirements that support successful delivery of the broader construction program. Executive Panel and Q&A: A moderator-led discussion with USMMA leadership, USACE program representatives, and USACE Contracting, including questions and topics submitted by industry. Doing Business with the Government: A practical session presented by the USACE Office of Small Business Programs. Campus Tour and Networking: A campus tour and opportunities to engage with program managers, technical staff, government representatives, community stakeholders, and industry peers. Advance Industry Questions: Industry partners may submit proposed questions or discussion topics for the executive panel to Zachery.A.Bernard@usace.army.mil no later than September 30, 2026. Registration and Access Information Registration is required for every attendee, regardless of affiliation or attendance method. Email the information below to Zachery.A.Bernard@usace.army.mil no later than 12:00 p.m. Eastern Time on Monday, October 12, 2026. Use the subject line "USMMA FY27 Industry Day Registration." One representative may register multiple attendees, but the required information must be provided separately for each person. Full legal name of each attendee Organization, company, or other affiliation, if applicable Individual email address and telephone number for each attendee Attendance method: in person or virtual Company website, if applicable Current capability statement for industry participants Virtual Attendance: A Microsoft Teams link will be emailed to registered virtual attendees on October 13, 2026. In-person attendance is strongly encouraged. Campus Access Requirements All in-person attendees must present a valid REAL ID-compliant credential or another form of government-issued photo identification acceptable to USMMA security and comply with all campus-entry instructions provided to registered attendees. Logistics and Parking Campus Entrance: Use the main gate at 300 Steamboat Road, Kings Point, NY 11024. Parking: Free attendee parking is available in Marvin Lot; overnight parking is not permitted. Arrival: Check-in opens at 10:00 a.m. Allow time to enter, park, and walk to the event location; arrive no later than 10:45 a.m. for networking. On-Site Directions: Follow posted signs and directions from USMMA security and event personnel. Updates, Changes, and Cancellations Any material change to the schedule, format, access procedures, or event status will be announced through an amendment to this SAM.gov notice and by email to registered attendees. Notice Status and Disclaimer This announcement is for informational and advance-planning purposes only and is not a solicitation or Government commitment to award a contract. The Government will not reimburse costs associated with this notice or event. Attendance is not required to participate in a future acquisition, and all event information is subject to change. Primary Point of Contact Name: Zachery A. Bernard Title: Deputy, Office of Small Business Programs (OSBP) Organization: U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, North Atlantic Division - New York District Email: Zachery.A.Bernard@usace.army.mil Registration Email Subject: USMMA FY27 Industry Day Registration END OF SPECIAL NOTICE

title: RESERVE BASIN MAINTENANCE DREDGING CONTRACT FOR SITES AT THE PHILDELPHIA NAVY YARD IN THE PUBLIC WORKS DEPARTMENT PENNSYLVANIA AREA OF RESPONSIBILIY
description: The project consists of Maintenance Dredging within the North Side (Wharf N) of Reserve Basin and Schuylkill River Access Channel for the Government sites at the Philadelphia Navy Yard in the Public Works Department Pennsylvania area of responsibility. Maintenance dredging of approximately 96,611 cubic yards of sediment, using a sealed environmental clamshell bucket. Dredging within the Reserve Basin is in support of the Naval Support Activity Mechanicsburg, Philadelphia Navy Yard Annex. The Reserve Basin is being used to decommission various US Naval vessels. For the river pilots to be able to safely maneuver vessels through the Schuylkill River into the Reserve Basin berths and to ensure that tidal cycles will not cause sediment accumulation around the hulls making final removal very difficult, the berths need to be dredged to a minimum depth of -30 MLLW and a maximum over-dredge depth of -32 MLLW.

title: USCG Cutter Eagle New Dredging for Berthing at New London City Pier
description: Eagle Pier New Dredging (FY26) at New London�s City Pier, CT (NEW LONDON COUNTY), PSN #24014900. Contractor shall provide all personnel, equipment, materials, and all other items and services required to perform dredging of a new area immediately south of CGC EAGLE�s berth at New London�s City Pier. The intent is to deepen the area to allow tugboats to assist the cutter for mooring/unmooring at all tide levels. Requirements of the design specify dredging to a depth of -17.0� at Mean Lower Low Water (MLLW) +2.0� over dredging allowance. This equates to approximately 3,700 cubic yards (CY) of dredge spoils to remove to an upland disposal site. Offshore disposal is not permitted due to environmental sample analysis of the dredge area. There is an environmental time of year restriction in Connecticut that only permits dredging activities between October 1st and March 1st. SPECIAL NOTES: The contractor shall conduct dredging operations so that navigation through the channel is possible at all times. The scope of work also includes removals of approximately 50 piles that remain below the waterline. Any piles that cannot be fully removed are to be cut at -21.0� MLLW. Dredge quantity of 3,700 CY. This estimate is based on an average of the past annual dredging and surveys. The Contractor shall provide a cost for dredging per cubic yard. That per cubic yard cost will be used for any necessary contract cost adjustment resulting from dredging more or less than the estimated 3,700 cubic yards, within the limits of dredge. Contractor will be compensated for actual quantity of dredge material removed and disposed, within the limits of dredge, as shown on the plan sheets. Dredge disposal site location is to be determined by conditions of treated/non-treated piles for Base bid item and Option Bid item. The estimated value of the procurement is between $1,000,000 and $5,000,000. A 20% bid guarantee is required. Performance and Payment bonds will be required. The performance period is estimated to be 300 calendar days from issuance of Notice to Proceed. This acquisition is issued pursuant to FAR Part 14 Sealed Bidding and is 100% Set-Aside for Small Business concerns. All relevant solicitation documents, including specifications and drawings may be accessed for download beginning on the date of issue of the IFB at the following site: https://www.sam.gov. Vendors MUST be registered in the System for Award Management database through https://www.sam.gov in order to receive a federal government contract. title: Solicitation - Fort Hood GOCO Aircraft & Ground Fuel Services
description: Interested companies responding to the solicitation will be required to register in the System for Award Management (SAM) and Wide Area Workflow (WAWF). This is a follow-on solicitation notice to sources sought notice SPE603-25-R-5X24 and SPE603-25-R-0525. This solicitation notice is for Fuel Operations Services to include managing, maintaining, and operating Government-Owned, Contractor-Operated (GOCO) facilities and equipment at Ft. Hood, TX. The Contractor will ensure safe, accurate, and timely handling, quality control, and accountability of all Defense Working Capital Fund (DWCF)-owned petroleum products under their control. The Contractor will perform required maintenance to ensure facilities, associated systems, vehicles, and equipment remain operational to meet the base mission. The Contractor will comply with environmental protection, safety, and security directives. The Contractor will conduct required training to ensure personnel are fully qualified to perform Performance Work Statement (PWS) tasks. Tasks identified in the PWS are performed by either the Contractor or Government as specified in Section C-2.0 Performance Requirements. The Contractor shall conduct all necessary fuels operations to support base operations, airshows and special events, deployments, exercises, and contingencies under normal conditions, as well as, during periods of heightened security, inclement weather, or other unique situations. Operations must be safely and efficiently conducted to receive, store, transfer, issue, and account for products with appropriate controls to ensure fuel quality, maintain inventory accuracy, and ensure no environmental impact. The Contractor shall operate and maintain the self-service automated service station facilities, equipment, and systems and ensure sufficient product is available to provide 24 hours a day, seven days a week support of ground fuels. The Contractor shall perform required tasks to ensure fuel is properly accounted for and issued to only authorized users. The NAICS Code for this procurement is 493190 and will be 100% set aside for Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business. The period of performance is a four-year base period from December 1, 2026, through November 30, 2030, with a five-year option from December 1, 2030 through November 30, 2035, and a six-month option extension provision, December 1, 2035 through May 31, 2036. The Government anticipates awarding one Firm-Fixed Price contract. This information is subject to modification and in no way binds the Government to award a contract.

title: KC-135 Center Console Refresh (CCR) Revision 2
description: 12 August Amendment 02 to revise documents as a result of Q&A. 28 Jul 26 Amendment 01 to revised documents as a result of Q&A. 10 Jul 26 Center Console Refresh addresses critical obsolescence issues within the KC-135 Refueling Tanker aircraft. The US Air Force needs an updated Fuel System (FS), Flight Display System (FDS), and Flight Computer due to obsolescence and is looking for innovative ideas to not only replace but improve these systems with turn-key solutions enabling supportability and future growth. The FS, FDS, Flight Computer, and the future growth/adaptability define the scope of the CCR program. The program scope also includes the addition of autothrottle systems. The anticipated contract will be a Cost-Plus Incentive Fee (CPIF) for EMD, Firm Fixed Price (FFP) for Production and Deployment (P&D), single award indefinite delivery/quantity type contract comprised of One (1) 48-month Base Period with Six (6) 1-Year Option Periods and a projected period of performance from July 2028 to June 2038. description: The 319th Contracting Squadron at Grand Forks Air Force Base, ND is issuing this Request for Proposal (RFP) to award a Firm-Fixed-Price Requirements Contract for protective coating and painting services across base industrial facilities. title: Blanket Purchase Agreement of Laboratory Analyses Services for Worldwide Support
description: AMENDMENT 0002: this combined synopsis / solicitation has been amended, and the Small Business set-aside category has been broadened in order to promote more robust competition for these requirements, where the Government still intends to award multiple agreements for the requirement (as denoted in the attachment). Additionally, the ELIN attachment (Lab Services) have been updated, with a reduction in line items, as well to improve competition. As a result, any offeror that has previously submitted quotes for consideration will have to provide a new ELIN quote submittal, but are still elible for award consideration. At this time, the original proposal due date has been extended to April 30, 2026; were the Contracting Officer to issue any further amendments to the proposal information, they will be posted to this same public record for widest and most-timely distribution. AMENDMENT 0001: responses to RFI have been posted to close the RFI event, and historical data for informational purposes has been posted as well. This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial products or commercial services prepared in accordance with the format in subpart 12.6, as supplemented with additional information included in this notice (attachments). This announcement constitutes the only solicitation; proposals are being requested and a written solicitation will not be issued. The requiring activity has determined that establishment of Blanket Purchase Agreements (BPA) is both appropriate and would be advantageous, and as a result quotes are being sought for the establishment of long-term agreements as a result. Interested vendors shall prepare to furnish laboratory analyses services and associated laboratory supplies, if and when requested by the Contracting Officer (or the authorized Representative of the Contracting Officer) anticipated as (but limited to) five one-year periods starting in 2026. Attached to this advertisement are pre-award evaluation procedures, proposal requirements for responsiveness and responsibility determinations, and a full set of objectives and standards for future ordering and performance. The solicitation utilizes source selection procedures which require offerors to submit a technical proposal, past performance and experience information, and pricing quotes for evaluation by the Government; details of submittal and evaluation are listed at provisions 52.212-1 and 52.212-2, respectively. Additionally, please make note of the mandatory format for quoting pricing of laboratory analyses services and directly-associated laboratory supplies. Note: copies of NAVFAC Past Performance Questionnaire (PPQ) forms have been newly posted in the attachments as of December 29, 2025; in accordance with Federal regulations, the Government's preferred source of past performance are records at CPARS.gov (see FAR Subpart 42.15), but these PPQ forms may be used for state, municipal, and/or private sector projects that are appropriate as past performance. The Government will give fair consideration to all awardees in placing orders based on criteria stated in the solicitation. This will be a new procurement. It does not directly replace an existing contract. No prior contract information exists. Interested, eligible Small Business concerns should, as early as possible but not later than 15 days of this notice, indicate interest in the acquisition by providing to the contracting office above evidence of capability to perform and a positive statement of eligibility as a small business concern. title: Delivery and installation of a High ion density etcher for lithium niobate on insulator - LiNb03 (LN)
description: DTU Nanolab wishes to acquire a high ion density source reactive ion etcher for etching lithium niobate on insulator 150 mm wafer processing. Delivery is expected no later than Q4 2027. We are looking for a highly versatile instrument providing stable etch recipes, capable of etching at both nanometer scale and micrometer scale with precise control of etching depth, typically a few hundreds of nm. The instrument must have state-of-the-art performance in terms of profile control, uniformity, selectivity, and in particu-lar etching sidewall smoothness to achieve low waveguide loss. The Instrument will be installed in the DTU Nanolab cleanroom - a university facility providing a comprehensive suite of micro- and nanofabrication tools. It serves a diverse community of over 200 active users, ranging from novice students to experienced researchers, as well a high percentage of commercial clients. At DTU Nanolab there are several research groups and companies working on developing and running small scale production of optical devises on the tools. Therefor the capability of etching smooth optical waveguide, gratings and other low-roughness optical devises are of high importance to us.

title: BUD-TBA Böckten - Hauptstrasse, Ingenieurleistungen einschliesslich Bauleitung SIA-Phasen 41-53
description:
Le marché porte sur les prestations d’ingénierie nécessaires à la remise en état de la Hauptstrasse à Böckten, sur un tronçon d’environ 820 mètres compris entre le pont sur l’Ergolz et la limite communale avec Gelterkinden. Le projet comprend notamment le remplacement complet de la superstructure routière, l’aménagement des trottoirs et des arrêts de bus, la rénovation du système d’évacuation des eaux de chaussée ainsi que divers travaux relatifs aux réseaux de conduites.

Le mandat comprend l’examen du projet de l’ouvrage existant ainsi que les prestations correspondant aux phases SIA 41 et 51 à 53. Celles-ci comprennent notamment l’appel d’offres et l’adjudication des travaux de construction, l’étude d’exécution, la coordination des parties prenantes et des propriétaires de réseaux, la direction des travaux, la mise en service, l’élimination des défauts et l’établissement du décompte final.

You must be the current owner of the building or a brokers representative of the existing owner. title: 2026 Albuquerque Area IHS Native American-Owned Small Business Industry Day
description: ? Celebrating Our 6th Annual Industry Day � Connecting Native-Owned Businesses with Albuquerque Area Indian Health Service (IHS) ? Monday, September 28 & Tuesday, September 29, 2026 ? 9:00 a.m. � 3:00 p.m. Mountain Daylight Time (MDT) ? Virtual Event | Microsoft Teams ?? FREE to Participate ? Space is limited. Registration will close once all vendor presentation slots have been filled. The Albuquerque Area Indian Health Service (IHS), Division of Contracts and Grants Management (DCGM), invites Native American-owned small businesses to participate in the 2026 Albuquerque Area IHS Native American-Owned Small Business Industry Day, a two-day virtual event dedicated to strengthening partnerships, expanding the Albuquerque Area IHS supplier base, and increasing awareness of the capabilities of Native American-owned businesses. Held shortly before Indigenous Peoples� Day, this event provides Native American-owned small businesses, including eligible Small Business Indian Firms (SBIFs) and Indian Small Business Economic Enterprises (ISBEEs), an opportunity to introduce their organizations and showcase their capabilities directly to Albuquerque Area IHS acquisition professionals, program stakeholders, and organizational leadership. ?? Event Overview Day One will begin with introductions from Albuquerque Area IHS acquisition professionals and a brief overview of the Buy Indian Act and its role in supporting Indian economic enterprises through federal procurement. Following the opening session, participating vendors will receive an individually scheduled 10-minute presentation slot to introduce their businesses and highlight their capabilities, qualifications, products, services, past performance, and other information relevant to potential Albuquerque Area IHS requirements. Vendor capability presentations will continue throughout both days. ? Vendor Capability Presentations This is your opportunity to show Albuquerque Area IHS what your business can do! Each participating vendor will receive 10 minutes to present its capabilities directly to Albuquerque Area IHS personnel and other invited IHS acquisition and program professionals. Vendors are encouraged to use their presentation time to highlight information such as: Core capabilities and areas of expertise Products and/or services offered Relevant experience and past performance Geographic areas served Unique capabilities or solutions How your business can support IHS healthcare operations and mission requirements ? Who Will Be in the Audience? The Industry Day is designed to connect Native American-owned businesses with Albuquerque Area IHS personnel and other invited IHS acquisition and program professionals involved in identifying requirements, conducting market research, planning acquisitions, making purchases, and administering contracts. The audience may include: Buyers Contract Specialists Contracting Officers Contracting Officer�s Representatives (CORs) Government Purchase Cardholders and Approving Officials Service Unit Chief Executive Officers Program and technical personnel Albuquerque Area leadership This broad audience provides participating businesses an opportunity to increase awareness of their capabilities across IHS while helping acquisition and program personnel identify potential sources for future requirements. ? Why Participate? The Albuquerque Area IHS is committed to meaningful industry engagement and expanding opportunities for Native American-owned small businesses. Participation in Industry Day provides businesses an opportunity to: Introduce their company directly to IHS acquisition, program, and organizational personnel Increase awareness of their products, services, and capabilities Help IHS identify new and emerging industry capabilities Support IHS market research and acquisition planning Develop relationships with acquisition and program personnel Increase awareness of potential opportunities to do business with IHS At the same time, these interactions help Albuquerque Area IHS broaden its procurement base, identify qualified sources, increase competition, and strengthen relationships with the Native American-owned business community. We want to learn what your business can do for IHS. ? How to Participate Native American-owned small businesses interested in participating should email: ALBAreaSmallBusiness@ihs.gov Please indicate your interest in participating in the 2026 Albuquerque Area IHS Native American-Owned Small Business Industry Day and include your business name and primary point of contact. Upon receipt of your email, the Albuquerque Area IHS will provide a registration form to collect additional business information and assist with scheduling. Presentation times will be scheduled in advance. Each participating vendor will receive 10 minutes to present its capabilities, qualifications, products, and/or services. Space is limited, and registration will close once all available vendor presentation slots have been filled. Vendors are encouraged to register early. Additional event and Microsoft Teams information will be provided to registered participants prior to the event. ? Building Partnerships in Support of the IHS Mission Through the 2026 Albuquerque Area IHS Native American-Owned Small Business Industry Day, DCGM seeks to strengthen relationships with Native American-owned businesses, expand awareness of industry capabilities, broaden the Albuquerque Area procurement base, and identify qualified sources capable of supporting healthcare delivery. These partnerships help ensure that Albuquerque Area IHS acquisition professionals have access to capable and innovative businesses that can provide the supplies, services, equipment, and solutions necessary to support direct patient care and advance the IHS mission: �To raise the physical, mental, social and spiritual health of American Indians and Alaska Natives to the highest level.� ? Join us September 28-29, 2026, and show Albuquerque Area IHS what your business can do! ?? Important Notice This Industry Day is being conducted for informational, outreach, and market research purposes. This event is not a bidder�s conference, solicitation, Request for Proposal, Request for Quote, promise to contract, or commitment by the Government to award a contract. Participation in this event does not guarantee consideration for or award of any future procurement. The Government will not assume liability for costs incurred by any participant associated with attending the event or preparing, submitting, or presenting information, capability statements, presentations, or other materials. Costs incurred in response to this notice will not be considered allowable direct or indirect charges to the Government.

title: Netherlands – Laboratory, optical and precision equipments (excl. glasses) – Supply and Analysis of NH₃ Passive Samplers (Diffusion Tubes) for the MAN Network and additional projects
description: This European tender concerns a contract for the supply and laboratory analysis of ammonia (NH₃) passive samplers (diffusion tubes) for the Dutch ammonia monitoring network “Meetnet Ammoniak Nederland” (MAN) and various additional projects. The contractor will be responsible for the monthly supply of unexposed diffusion tubes to RIVM, the analysis of exposed tubes supplied by RIVM, and the digital reporting of validated results. Field deployment, return logistics of exposed tubes and internal data processing by RIVM fall outside the scope. The expected annual volume ranges from approximately 6,600 tubes in the baseline MAN scenario up to around 9,900 tubes including additional projects, with a maximum bandwidth of up to 30,000 tubes per year to accommodate future growth. If the contract is awarded to a new supplier, the first contract year will include a structured Double Measurement Programme, in which the new laboratory’s performance is systematically compared with the current trend laboratory to ensure continuity and trend stability in the MAN data series. The contract is tendered as one single, integrated lot combining tube supply, analysis and reporting with one contractor, using a best price‑quality ratio award criterion. The agreement has a fixed initial duration of six (6) years starting 1 January 2027, with five (5) optional one‑year extensions, for a maximum total duration of eleven (11) years.

description: Le périmètre du projet se situe sur le tronçon de route nationale N05.80, entre Bözingenfeld et Lengnau, et couvre la partie allant de l’échangeur de Bözingenfeld jusqu’à l’objet Pont de Leugene (BS 20), soit du km 73.965 au km 81.195. Il s’étend ainsi sur une longueur de 7,23 km. Le tronçon partiel de la N16 entre l’échangeur de Bözingenfeld et l’ouvrage Pont sur T5 (D01) fait partie du tronçon d’entretien N05.80. Ce dernier été construit en grande partie entre 1998 et 2000, puis mis en service en 2001. Le passage inférieur Bözingenfeld sur la N16 (BS 03) a été construit en 2020. Il s’agit de la route nationale N05, de 1re classe, qui appartient à l’OFROU. Le périmètre du projet inclut 8 passages supérieurs, 4 passages inférieurs, 4 ponceaux, 1 cuve, 6 murs de soutènement, 1 tunnel, 5 digues antibruit, 5 parois antibruit, 2 bassins de rétention d’hydrocarbures, 2 puits de pompage et 20 portiques de signalisation. Les travaux de rénovation comprennent le remplacement du revêtement sur l’ensemble du tronçon, la rénovation des 4 bassins de rétention des eaux pluviales, divers travaux de réfection du béton sur des ouvrages d’art et dans le tunnel de Pieterlen, le renforcement localisé de certains poteaux de signalisation, divers traitements hydrophobes sur des ouvrages d’art, le remplacement du système de protection des surfaces dans le tunnel de Pieterlen, le marquage, la signalisation et l’éclairage sur l’ensemble du tronçon. Par ailleurs, les conditions de circulation des points noirs identifiés à Bienne-Est / échangeur de Bözingenfeld et à Lengnau feront l’objet d’une analyse technique. Des travaux d’aménagement sont prévus. Le présent appel d’offres porte sur les prestations d’auteur du projet Environnement (SER et bruit compris) pour les phases allant du concept d’intervention / projet définitif, comprenant la procédure d’approbation des plans (accompagnement de la procédure et traitement des oppositions), jusqu’à la réalisation / mise en service (en option). Ces prestations devront être réalisées selon la méthode de planification BIM.

title: Germany – Building-cleaning services – Gebäudeinnenreinigung von 4 Schulen in Bremen
description: Ziel dieser Ausschreibung ist es, einen geeigneten Auftragnehmer für die Gebäudeinnenreinigung von vier Schulen zu finden. Dies beinhaltet die fachgerechte Gebäudeinnenreinigung der im Raumbuch jeweils enthaltenen Raumgruppen sowie dieerforderlichen Maßnahmen zur Pflege und Werterhaltung. Außerdem wird die Bereitschaft für zusätzliche Sonderreinigungen und -leistungen nach schriftlicher Anordnung vorausgesetzt. Die zu reinigenden Gesamtflächen betragen im Jahr 946.696,08m² (Oberschule an der Helgolander Straße), 901.086,96m² (Marie-Curie-Schule), 769.884,60m² (Schule Oberneuland) und 600.528,43m² (Kippenberg-Gymnasium). Objektbegehungen finden am 12.10.2026 um 10:00 Uhr (Oberschule an der Helgolander Straße), am 13.10.2026 um 10:00 Uhr (Schule Oberneuland), am 13.10.2026 um 11:30 Uhr (Marie-Curie-Schule) und am 14.10.2026 um 10:00 Uhr (Kippenberg-Gymnasium) statt. Die Begehung der Gebäude ist verpflichtend; eine Nichtteilnahme führt zum Ausschluss vom Vergabeverfahren bezogen auf das jeweilige Los. Sollten Sie also bspw. ausschließlich bei der Begehung am 12.10.2026 teilnehmen, werden Angebote für die Lose 2, 3 und 4 von der Wertung ausgeschlossen und nur das Angebot für Los 1 gewertet. Eine Anmeldung ist nur bis zum 09.10.2026 um 12:00 Uhr möglich. Bitte melden Sie sich per E-Mail an: gebaeudeservice@immobilien.bremen.de Nach der Anmeldung erhalten Sie eine Bestätigung mit weiteren Details (u.a. zum Treffpunkt). Bitte teilen Sie uns auch mit, an welchen der vier Begehungen Sie teilnehmen möchten (alle oder nur einzelne). Waschmaschinenanschlüsse sind in der Marie-Curie-Schule, der Schule Oberneuland und im Kippenberg-Gymnasium vorhanden. In der Oberschule an der Helgolander Straße gibt es keine Waschmaschinenanschlüsse. Reinigungsfenster: Nach Absprache innerhalb der zuschlagsfreien Zeiten zwischen 05:00 und 22:00 Uhr. Weitere Details zur Beschreibung der Beschaffung finden Sie in den Vergabeunterlagen in der Leistungsbeschreibung und im Leistungsverzeichnis. Die Vergabestelle behält sich vor, Angebote, deren effektiver Stundenverrechnungssatz (einschließlich aller gewährten Nachlässe) unter 180% des derzeit gültigen Tariflohnes liegt und damit unauskömmlich erscheint, vertieft zu prüfen. Angebote, deren effektiver Stundenverrechnungssatz unter 170% des derzeit gültigen Tariflohnes liegt, erscheinen automatisch unauskömmlich und werden direkt ohne weitere Prüfung ausgeschlossen. Die Vergabestelle fordert daher alle Bieter auf, den dem Angebot zugrunde liegenden Stundenverrechnungssatz gemäß dem Schema des Bundesinnungsverbandes Gebäudereinigung darzustellen und die Auskömmlichkeit des Angebots in den Einzelbestandteilen nachzuweisen. Dieses Schema ist dem Angebot beizufügen. Soweit die Zweifel an der Auskömmlichkeit im Rahmen der vertieften Prüfung nicht vollständig ausgeräumt werden können, wird das Angebot von der weiteren Wertung ausgeschlossen. Dies gilt auch dann, wenn der Bieter seiner Aufklärungspflicht nicht oder nicht in der Form nachkommt, dass rückfragefrei erkennbar und mit Nachweisen belegt wird, dass alle Kostenpositionen analog branchenüblicher Standards transparent hergeleitet wurden. Wir bitten aufgrund der Unsicherheit bezüglich des tariflichen Mindestlohns ab dem 01.01.2027 darum, den SVS weiterhin mit dem aktuellen tariflichen Mindestlohn von 15,00€ zu kalkulieren.
